decisions.claim: B is out of milk (along with A)
decisions.reason: A says 'We're out of milk' which presupposes B is part of the 'we' household. The claim correctly captures this presupposition.

decisions.claim: B is asked to go to the store to pick up items for the household
decisions.reason: A explicitly asks B to run to the store and says 'We need a few things,' presupposing B is part of the household needing items. B is being asked, not confirmed as having gone.

decisions.claim: B is part of the household that is out of milk
decisions.reason: Same presupposition from 'We're out of milk' as c1. c1 is the more complete representative of this fact.

decisions.claim: B is part of the household that needs sugar, oranges, and milk
decisions.reason: Same 'we' presupposition from turn 3 as c2. c2 already captures B's household membership with the shopping context.

decisions.claim: B has money available to purchase the items
decisions.reason: A asks 'Do you have enough money?' which does NOT establish B has money. A question does not confirm its answer; B could lack money.
decisions.counterexample: B might not have enough money, prompting A to offer cash.

decisions.claim: B agreed to do the favor of going to the store
decisions.reason: A's 'Thanks very much' is a polite closing formula. It does not confirm B agreed or completed the task. A could be thanking in advance or closing the conversation regardless.
decisions.counterexample: B might have declined and A still said thanks politely.

decisions.claim: B asked how many oranges were needed
decisions.reason: Turn 9 'Oh, let's see... About six' is A's own answer to an unseen B question. We cannot confirm B asked about oranges specifically; A might be self-correcting or answering a different query.
decisions.counterexample: B might have asked about sugar quantity, and A answered about oranges unprompted.

decisions.claim: B asked about the quantity of milk needed
decisions.reason: Turn 13 'No. I think a half gallon will be enough' is A's response. We cannot confirm B asked about milk quantity; B might have asked about sugar or something else.
decisions.counterexample: B might have asked 'Do we need a gallon?' about a different item.

decisions.claim: B is physically present and able to travel to the store
decisions.reason: 'Could you run over to the store?' presupposes B is physically present and capable of travel. This is a genuine E2 presupposition from the request.

decisions.claim: B was asked to pick up a small bag of sugar specifically
decisions.reason: A explicitly requests sugar (turn 5) and specifies 'A small bag' (turn 7). This is a direct instruction to B about what to purchase.

decisions.claim: B was asked to confirm they understood the complete shopping list
decisions.reason: A asks 'Have you got all that?' (turn 15), presupposing B is expected to confirm understanding of the shopping list. This is a genuine presupposition from the question.
